quests.sentence: The reports are reviewed every month.
quests.hint: The thing receiving the action becomes the subject, followed by is/are plus the past participle.
quests.explanation: The reports (the thing acted upon) becomes the subject, followed by are reviewed — the passive shifts focus from who reviews to what gets reviewed.

quests.sentence: English is spoken in many countries.
quests.hint: The passive works well when the doer is unimportant or unknown — here, who speaks English isn't the point.
quests.explanation: English is spoken shifts focus onto the language itself rather than any specific speaker, which is why no agent is mentioned.

quests.sentence: The packages are delivered by the courier.
quests.hint: By plus the doer can still follow the past participle when the agent is worth naming.
quests.explanation: By the courier names the agent doing the delivering, following are delivered — the passive form still allows the agent when it's relevant.

quests.sentence: The building was designed by a famous architect.
quests.hint: The past passive uses was/were plus the past participle, with by naming a specific, notable agent.
quests.explanation: Was designed uses the past passive form, and by a famous architect names an agent worth mentioning because it adds important information.

quests.sentence: The contract was signed yesterday.
quests.hint: The past passive can also close with a time word instead of an agent.
quests.explanation: Was signed uses the past passive form, with yesterday (time) closing the sentence instead of a by-agent.

quests.sentence: The results were announced this morning.
quests.hint: Were pairs with a plural subject in the past passive, the same way was does for singular.
quests.explanation: Were announced pairs the plural subject the results with the past passive form, followed by this morning (time).

quests.sentence: The novel was written by a young author.
quests.hint: Include the by-agent when knowing who did the action adds real, useful information.
quests.explanation: By a young author is included because knowing who wrote the novel matters to the reader — the agent is worth naming here.

quests.sentence: The window was broken.
quests.hint: Omit the by-agent entirely when the doer is unknown or simply doesn't matter.
quests.explanation: Was broken has no by-agent at all, since who broke the window is unknown or unimportant — the passive lets the sentence work without one.

quests.sentence: The award was presented by the mayor.
quests.hint: Include the agent again here, since knowing who presented the award is meaningful information.
quests.explanation: By the mayor is included because the presenter's identity matters, following was presented in the passive form.

quests.sentence: The form must be submitted by Friday.
quests.hint: A modal like must is followed by be plus the past participle, not is or was.
quests.explanation: Must be submitted inserts be right after the modal must, before the past participle submitted — modals always take be, never is/was, in the passive.

quests.sentence: This medicine should be taken with food.
quests.hint: The same modal-be-participle pattern applies with should, for advice.
quests.explanation: Should be taken inserts be after should, before the past participle taken, following the fixed modal-passive pattern.

quests.sentence: The issue can be resolved quickly.
quests.hint: Can also takes be plus the past participle in the passive, expressing ability or possibility.
quests.explanation: Can be resolved inserts be after can, before resolved, with quickly (manner) closing the sentence.

quests.sentence: The proposal has been finished.
quests.hint: Present perfect passive combines has/have with been, then the past participle — three parts in that order.
quests.explanation: Has been finished stacks has, been, and finished in that fixed order, linking a completed action to the present moment.
quests.grammarRule: Present Perfect Passive (Has/Have + Been + Past Participle)

quests.sentence: The documents have been reviewed.
quests.hint: Have pairs with been the same way for a plural subject.
quests.explanation: Have been reviewed stacks have, been, and reviewed for the plural subject the documents.
quests.grammarRule: Present Perfect Passive (Has/Have + Been + Past Participle)

quests.sentence: The building has been renovated recently.
quests.hint: The same three-part structure holds, with a time adverb closing the sentence.
quests.explanation: Has been renovated stacks has, been, and renovated, with recently closing the sentence.
quests.grammarRule: Present Perfect Passive (Has/Have + Been + Past Participle)

quests.sentence: The email was not sent.
quests.hint: Not slots in between was and the past participle, the same spot it takes in active be-negatives.
quests.explanation: Was not sent places not between was and the past participle sent, negating the passive action.

quests.sentence: The changes weren't approved.
quests.hint: Weren't fuses were and not, still sitting right before the past participle.
quests.explanation: Weren't approved fuses were and not into one word, right before the past participle approved.

quests.sentence: The order hasn't been shipped yet.
quests.hint: Hasn't been combines the negative contraction with been, before the past participle, plus yet at the end.
quests.explanation: Hasn't been shipped combines the negative present-perfect-passive form, with yet closing the sentence to emphasize it still hasn't happened.

quests.sentence: Was the report finished on time?
quests.hint: Move was to the front of the sentence, ahead of the subject, to ask the passive question.
quests.explanation: Was moves ahead of the report to form the question, with finished on time following in normal passive order.

quests.sentence: Is the software updated regularly?
quests.hint: Is inverts the same way for present passive questions, with the manner adverb at the end.
quests.explanation: Is opens the question before the software, with updated regularly completing it.

quests.sentence: Has the invoice been paid?
quests.hint: Has inverts to the front for a present-perfect-passive question, before been and the past participle.
quests.explanation: Has opens the question before the invoice, with been paid completing the present-perfect-passive question.

quests.sentence: When was the decision made?
quests.hint: The question word leads, then was, then the subject, then the past participle.
quests.explanation: When opens the question, was follows, the decision is the subject, and made completes the passive question.

quests.sentence: Where was this photo taken?
quests.hint: Where comes first, then was, then the subject, then the past participle.
quests.explanation: Where leads the question, was follows, this photo is the subject, and taken completes it.

quests.sentence: Why was the meeting postponed?
quests.hint: Why still opens the question, followed by was, the subject, and the past participle.
quests.explanation: Why leads the question, was follows, the meeting is the subject, and postponed completes it.

quests.sentence: The company laid off fifty employees.
quests.hint: An active sentence puts the doer first, as the subject, right before the verb.
quests.explanation: The company (the doer) is the subject here, acting directly on fifty employees — this is the active voice, focusing on who did the action.

quests.sentence: Fifty employees were laid off.
quests.hint: The passive version puts the receiver of the action first instead, dropping the agent entirely.
quests.explanation: Fifty employees (the receiver of the action) becomes the subject here, with the doer the company dropped entirely — a natural passive choice when the affected people matter more than who did it.

quests.sentence: The proposal was rejected by the board.
quests.hint: The passive can also keep the agent, when naming who made the decision still matters.
quests.explanation: By the board names the agent who rejected the proposal, showing the passive can include an agent when it's still relevant information.

quests.sentence: All applications must be submitted before the deadline.
quests.hint: Combine a modal passive with a before-time deadline at the end.
quests.explanation: Must be submitted uses the modal-passive pattern, with before the deadline closing the sentence as the time limit.

quests.sentence: The new policy has been approved by senior management.
quests.hint: Combine present perfect passive with a by-agent, common in formal workplace announcements.
quests.explanation: Has been approved uses the present-perfect-passive pattern, with by senior management naming the agent, typical of formal workplace language.

quests.sentence: Was the shipment delayed because of bad weather?
quests.hint: Combine a passive question with a because-of reason phrase at the end.
quests.explanation: Was delayed inverts to form the question, with because of bad weather explaining the reason at the end.
